Imold’s R&D department has expertise in mechanical design, industrial automation, mechatronics and CNC programming.
Imold is currently engaged in its own research topics concerning vision systems, AI, robotics.

entityDescription:
PLOATECH specializes in advanced scientific and customized engineering services, with a primary focus on the underwater domain. Our expertise spans in the following key sectors: remote sensing, data processing, instrumentation R&D, and robotics.
Data services include organizing and conducting survey operations with manned and/or robotic vehicles; real-time and post-processing 3D spatial measurements of the seafloor and water column, including temporal and multi-parametric data. Instrumentation R&D includes automations, scientific sensors, and systems integration. In addition, development and improvements of human-occupied submersibles, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs).

PLOATECH works to provide scientists with tools for detection and measurements, for helping improve the environmental conditions of the seas and oceans. To this end and although PLOATECH is a relatively new company, it draws over 25 years of experience in the marine scientific sector, and our track record includes participation in oceanographic expeditions and research projects funded by organizations such as H2020, NSF, NASA, and NOPP.
Space programs can directly benefit from technologies used for sea surface and underwater environments, either for data validation (ground truth) or as testbed for exploration in other ocean worlds. KanopyMed was founded in 2018 by Grégoire Mercier, a physician, and Ulysse Rodts, an economist, as a spin-off from the Montpellier University Hospital's innovation center.
The company's ambition is to improve the quality, efficiency, and equity of healthcare systems through population (public health) and individual (digital medical devices) approaches. 
Kanopymed implements innovative methodologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, dynamic mapping) to design decision support tools powered by health data (SNDS, registries, hospital data, open data).
Kanopymed places ethics at the heart of its values and is a founding member of EKITIA.
 
Key dates:
- In 2019, Kanopymed is a finalist in the AHRQ data challenge in the US.
- In 2020, the company signs several collaborations with major players in the pharmaceutical and medical device industries.
- In 2021, KanopyMed secures 250,000 euros in funding to develop PREDIC, a future digital medical device for cardiology.
- In April 2022, the company will partner with the Montpellier Metropolis and the Montpellier University Hospital to develop AIR-MAP, a digital twin of the metropolitan population to better understand the impact of air pollution on health.
- Coming soon: Medical CE marking for PREDIC and collaborations with companies.
 
The company is based in Montpellier and has four employees.

SkyWatch, a Canadian SME, that specializes in Earth observation (EO) data and the support of analytics, both through its state-of-the-art cloud-based software Platform. SkyWatch delivers pioneering solutions for both downstream and upstream space markets, focusing on the strategic needs of end users and customers. The Platform streamlines access to a comprehensive aggregation of satellite and aerial imagery, enabling rapid, on-demand processing and analysis, supporting applications requiring timely and accurate EO data - supporting dual-use applications. 
For the downstream, SkyWatch offers unparalleled ease in accessing and integrating EO data, supported by a scalable infrastructure and a robust API for seamless system integration. Since 2018, the Platform has gained traction with over 5,000 commercial organizations globally, evidencing its reliability and efficiency with over 1 million API calls per month, while offering its users to over 90% of commercially available satellite-based EO data. Additionally, SkyWatch specializes in the streamlined ingestion and integration of geospatial data products into any Esri environment or application. 
For the upstream, SkyWatch provides a tailored solution for satellite operators, facilitating efficient data management and monetization through a framework for creating data pipelines, while automating the entire process of data ingestion, processing, and distribution. The Platform excels in high-volume data processing and supports the integration of machine learning and AI models, resulting in less waste and lower costs for operators. The Platform leverages market intelligence from the downstream, creating tactical and strategic benefits for operators to optimize collections, plan orbits, engage in speculative tasking, and increase fulfillment. 
Over the past 10 years of operation, we've developed have a strong set of competences around multi-sensor integration, orchestration, data management & storage, and delivery to workflows that benefits our private commercial customer base, while also engaging with the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) and the European Space Agency (ESA) on key strategic R&D projects.

entityDescription:
ReLUIS 
 
Competence Center of the Civil Protection Department - decree of the Department Chief n.3152 of 24 July 2013, published on the Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 220 of 19 September 2013
 
The Laboratories University Network of seismic engineering (Rete dei Laboratori Universitari di Ingegneria Sismica - ReLUIS), founded through a conventional act signed on the 17th of April of 2003, is a interuniversity consortium with the purpose to co-ordinate the activity of earthquake engineering University Laboratories, giving scientific, organizational, technical and financial supports to associated University while promoting their participation to scientific and technological-orientated activities in earthquake engineering field, in accordance with national and international research plans in this area.
Co-ordination action promotes the partnerships between Universities, Private Universities, and Inter-university Centres (henceforth indicated with the term “University”) and between them and other Research Institutes and Industries and also promotes the development of earthquake engineering Laboratories according to its statute, through conducting generation and dissemination of knowledge.
The consortium is a scientific interlocutor of different Governmental, Regional, Provincial and Council Agencies and of public and private Institutes to get tangible objectives concerning vulnerability and risk evaluation and reduction.
All the scholars belonging to the associated consortium structures, at the moment of acknowledgment to the consortium or belonging to the foundation for founder members, that take care of problems concerning seismic engineering, can associate and participate in Consortium activities by co-operating in an interdisciplinary way.
The consortium has the main office in Naples in the Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture, University of Naples “Federico II”. The consortium is a nonprofit organization.
Founder and pertaining members are:
University of Basilicata (Dep. of Structures, Geotechnical and Engineering Geology)
University of Naples Federico II (Dep. of Civil Engineering and Architecture)
University of Pavia (Dep. of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering)
Successive members:
University of Trento (Dip. of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering)
In addition to partner universities, experts and professors belonging to further universities and research institutes, well widespread on the national territory, as shown in the figure below, participate to the research and support activities of the Consortium.

entityDescription: The Stochastic Hydrogeology Lab is a research unit within the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Neuchâtel. It develops mathematical methods and software in the field of spatio-temporal statistics. These methods are used to interpolate properties based on observations and quantify uncertainty. This team is among the world leader in the field of multiple-point statisticis, which is a branch of spatial statistics that build models by learning from example. It is a category of machine learning method able to produce patterns in space or time that are similar to those observed in analog data. These methods can be used to reconstruct the spatial distribution of rock types in the undeground, fill missing data gaps in remote sensing observation, or model time series.
